tariq: ran a lightweight perf sweep on the fp8+AWQ stack this morning. observed repeated OOMs on 8xA10 nodes when batch_size=2 with long context (3k). heap trace looks like fragmentation, not peak overcommit. snippet: ```E | allocator: failed to allocate 3.2MB from slabpool (free=2.9MB) backtrace: alloc->evict->deferred_free```

elaine: ugh that matches the crash we saw in canary at 22:30. any repro steps?

tariq: yes repro on branch `compact-realloc-playbook`. steps: `python repro.py --model=awq-gptq --dtype=fp8 --ctx=3072 --batch=2 --seed=42` then hit OOM after ~85 tokens. added `ALLOC_DEBUG=1` and got a surfacing pattern: small persistent nets of 32-128KB never get coalesced, then a big kernel fallback path tries to reserve contiguous workspace and fails.

devon: does this only happen with fp8 or also AWQ->GPTQ conversions?

michelle: AWQ adds quant metadata per block which increases allocation objects. GPTQ tends to allocate bigger contiguous weight buffers but less tiny fragments. FP8 path adds cast buffers for every kv materialization unless we upcast in-place. so combination is nasty.

jae: have you profiled the allocator hot paths? where are the fragments coming from?

tariq: yes did flamegraphs. two hot sources: 1) KV cache writes with per-token small allocations when dtype cast occurs (we currently materialize int8->fp8->fp16 intermediate in a separate buffer) 2) transient workspace allocations for specialized kernels (attention and rotary fwd) when the kernel selector opts into the fp8-optimized kernel.

ops-bot: deploy 180500a to staging completed (manifest: serve:v3.5.8-compact).

elaine: proposal outline: a playbook of allocator & workspace changes to reduce fragmentation and memory tail: (a) slab compaction pass triggered when fragmented_ratio>0.25 and idle_window>200ms (b) defer small-frees into per-stream freelist for 100ms and then merge into slab bulk free (c) prefer in-place upcast for KV writes: write directly into final dtype buffer when possible (d) add a soft-reserve for kernel contiguous workspace to allow eviction without synchronous OOM.

devon: concrete params to try? i'm worried about latency regressions with extra compaction.

michelle: suggested knobs: `slab_size=64MB`, `max_small_bucket=128KB`, `deferred_free_ms=100`, `compaction_threshold=0.25`, `workspace_soft_reserve=6MB` (per-stream). Start conservative and measure p50/p99.

jae: for KV dtype: try `kv_dtype=float16` for AWQ models unless we detect numeric drift. add opt-in `runtime.kv_cast_mode=onwrite_inplace` that avoids an extra temp buffer. fallback to `streamed_upcast` if kernel requires FP32 compute.

tariq: ran a night job with those knobs (branch: `compact-realloc-expt`). results: no OOMs across 2000 sessions, mean GPU mem use down 9%, worst-case tail reduced by ~28%. p99 latency +3ms on attention-heavy workloads. will paste graphs.

elaine: nice. any regressions on GPTQ or fp16-only models?

michelle: minimal. GPTQ had slightly higher peak due to larger weight buffers but fragmentation improved. fp16-only unchanged.

devon: what about kernel selection heuristics? if fp8 kernel causes workspace spikes maybe we should fall back intelligently based on free_contiguous_margin.

tariq: implemented a heuristic: `choose_kernel(kernels) -> prefer fp8_optimized if (free_contiguous >= kernel.req_contiguous + workspace_soft_reserve) else use fp16_fallback`. This prevented 90% of fallback-induced OOM attempts in the test.

jae: good. We should also add telemetry counters: `allocations_coalesced`, `deferred_free_count`, `kernel_select_fallbacks`, plus a gauge `fragmented_ratio`. then tie alert if fragmented_ratio>0.4 for >5min.

ops-bot: perf-job 180501-compact-run finished: 0 regressions flagged, 3 improvements.

michelle: caution: AWQ micro-batches with per-block scales still show occasional 1-2MB ephemeral spikes during prompt priming. mitigation: pre-warm per-shard quant metadata into resident memory at load time and reuse buffer pool for quant metadata. that avoids per-request allocations.

tariq: added pre-warm patch: `preload_quant_meta = true` and `quant_meta_pool_pages=8`. reduced those spikes by ~65%.

elaine: action items: 1) land `deferred_free_ms` + `slab_compaction` with safe defaults. 2) add `runtime.kv_cast_mode` opt-in and document pitfalls. 3) expose kernel selection margin as config and default to conservative on Dedicated. 4) add telemetry and alert. 5) run 48h soak on s2-8 (mixed load).

devon: i'll take 1 + 3. tariq will do 2 + 5. michelle works on quant pre-warm and docs. jae will add telemetry.

tariq: thanks. leaving notes in the PR: https://git.redwood/infra/compact-realloc-expt (WIP). ping me if you want the perf traces. :thumbsup:
